title: Component Maintenance Roadmap and Review Rotation (tokens, buttons, tables, charts)
creator: Maya Chen
description: Objective: Establish an operational pattern for ongoing maintenance of core primitives (tokens, buttons, tables, charts) that combines a lightweight RFC process, a cross-functional review rotation, and a clear staged deprecation policy. This ticket captures the proposed cadence, templates, review checklist, migration guidance, and follow-up actions required to keep the component library safe for downstream apps while enabling evolution.
background: Recent incidents: two unexpected visual regressions after token changes (see links) and long-lived PRs waiting on design review. Current governance documents are fragmented across Confluence and Drive; teams find the deprecation windows unclear. We need a concise, enforceable process that minimizes consumer surprise and maintenance burden.
goals: Define a monthly review rotation for component owners and reviewers
Create a 1-page RFC template for fast component changes and a separate token-change template
Publish an explicit deprecation timeline with automation hooks (lint warnings, console banners)
Add a practical reviewer checklist covering accessibility, tokens, semantic versioning, and migration cost
Document roll-forward and fallback steps for emergency rollbacks
deliverables: Review rotation schedule and on-call roster (6-week cadence)
RFC templates: component-rfc.md and token-change-rfc.md in repo/docs
Reviewer checklist (to be added as CODEOWNERS guidance and PR template)
Deprecation policy with automated warnings and migration notes
Communication plan and example notices for consuming teams
review_rotation_model: Each core area (tokens, inputs/buttons, tables, charts) will nominate two rotating reviewers: a design lead and one engineer. Rotation runs 6 weeks; responsibility includes triaging incoming RFCs/PRs, approving non-breaking changes, and convening a 30-minute weekly sync during active sprints.
rfc_templates_summary: Lightweight RFC (component-rfc.md): purpose, backwards-compatibility assessment, owner, migration footprint, telemetry flags, rollout plan, test cases. Token-change-rfc.md: token provenance, affected tokens list, aliasing recommendations, visual regression checklist, canary rollout guidance.
deprecation_policy_summary: Staged approach: Notice (90 days) -> Shim & Lint (60 days) -> Deprecation flag & docs update (30 days) -> Removal (after 180 total days from first notice). Emergency removals require cross-team approval and an explicit rollback plan. Deprecation notices must include migration snippets and a codemod where feasible.
review_checklist: Visual: screenshot diffs across default and dark themes, token deltas documented
Accessibility: keyboard, focus states, color contrast scores, aria roles
Token hygiene: avoid new hard-coded values; prefer token aliases and semantic names
API stability: props documented, breaking changes flagged with major-version guidance
Telemetry and errors: ensure feature flags and metrics for rollout
Perf: snapshot render cost for tables and charts with 100/1000 rows where applicable
Docs: PR includes updated examples and migration notes
Testing: storybook story + unit snapshot + visual regression test
Release: include release notes entry and deprecation timeline if applicable
automation_and_linting: Add a CI job that warns on token removals and adds a 'deprecation' label to PRs that touch deprecated APIs. Enable an eslint rule in consuming apps to surface deprecated tokens at build time. Add a lightweight dashboard in Console that surfaces open RFCs and deprecations by consumer teams.
migration_guidance_examples: tokens: provide an alias mapping table and a small jscodeshift script example for replacing legacy token names
buttons: show before/after prop mappings and a feature flag example to toggle new behavior
tables: a progressive enhancement path for virtualized rows and API compatibility notes
charts: decouple data formatting logic into helper and keep render props stable
communication_plan: Announce RFCs and deprecation notices in #design-system Slack channel, weekly digest for platform teams, and a monthly email to integrators. All deprecation notices should link to migration PRs, codemods, and an issue tracker for blockers.
risks_and_tradeoffs: Tighter governance increases PR latency and could slow small UX fixes. We mitigate by making the RFC templates minimal, enabling reviewers to do 'fast-triage' for low-risk changes. Automated linting and codemods reduce manual work. Longer deprecation windows increase maintenance cost but reduce downstream outages.
acceptance_criteria: Rotation roster published and two rotations scheduled in calendar
RFC templates added to design-system/docs and referenced in PR template
Reviewer checklist added to PR template and CODEOWNERS guidance updated
Lint rule and CI warning for token removals merged (can be disabled via feature flag)
Deprecation communication template created and one example notice published
